title: I remade my 2023 game jam game in 30 minutes using a single AI prompt
author: Square-Yam-3772
selftext:
Back in 2023, I spent roughly 1 to 2 weeks building a small game for a jam.

Today, I described that exact same game in one *mega prompt*… and let AI rebuild it.

It took less than 30 minutes to get a playable version.

It’s not 1:1 (and still needs polish), but honestly… it’s close enough that it feels kind of surreal.

I’m starting to feel like building games is shifting from “writing everything to “describing what should exist”

Curious how other devs feel about this. Exciting or kind of unsettling?

comments.author: PlaidWorld
comments.body: To simplistic to care honestly.  Btw the original is really cute tho.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
The scary thing about this is that I can just reuse the same sprite and tileset if I want a more faithful remake 

I used to not take mega prompts seriously and now I realize that it is actually viable

Handling complexity is a question mark still. I am currently more comfortable iteraring piece by piece vs refining the entire thing as a whole but we will see

replies.author: umhassy
replies.body:
>I used to not take mega prompts seriously and now I realize that it is actually viable

I dont want to burst your bubble but the mega prompt can give you 80% of the game but players like the small details and the small details have to be done extra (either with extra prompts or whatever).

It's fast but its also soulless if you dont do the finetuning. Its like comparing a song which has the basic beats compared to a song which was fully remastered or sth.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
that's just a matter of polish though. I mean, people can spend a lot time with their games and still not get the level of polish they want

to be fair, speed isn't really a problem for me currently even with my usual approach of just prompt one thing at a time

replies.author: umhassy
replies.body: Which AI are you using and do you mind sharing your prompt or your prompt structure?

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I used google ai studio for this, after the mega prompt, I replace the placeholder with a sprite I generated

**Role:** You are an expert JavaScript developer specializing in Phaser 3 game development.

**Task:** Build a complete, single-file Phaser 3 game (using CDN for the library) based on the following specifications:

# 1. Game Overview

* **Theme:** Top-down 2D "Dino Rampage."
* **Controls:** WASD or Arrow Keys for movement.
* **Core Mechanic:** The dinosaur grows when eating people and shrinks when taking damage.

# 2. Entities & Behaviors

* **The Dinosaur (Player):** \* Starts at a scale of 1.0.
   * **Growth:** Increase scale by 0.05 for every person eaten (max scale 4.0).
   * **Shrink:** Decrease scale by 0.2 when hit by a tank shell or soldier bullet (min scale 0.5). If scale goes below 0.5, Game Over.
* **People (Prey):** \* Spawn randomly and move in erratic "panic" patterns.
   * Destroyed on collision with the Player.
* **Buildings (Destructibles):** \* Static objects.
   * When the Player collides with them, trigger a "crumble" effect (alpha fade or tint change) and disable their physics body.
* **Enemies (Tanks & Soldiers):** \* **Soldiers:** Small, slow-moving, fire low-damage projectiles at the player.
   * **Tanks:** Slower than soldiers but fire faster, larger projectiles.
   * They should keep a distance from the player and rotate to face them.

# 3. Technical Requirements

* **Physics:** Use Arcade Physics.
* **Scaling Logic:** Ensure the Player's physics body/hitbox scales dynamically with the sprite's visual scale.
* **Camera:** The camera must follow the player and zoom out slightly as the player gets larger.
* **Assets:** Since I don't have images yet, please use **Phaser Primitives (Rectangles/Circles)** or basic colored placeholders so the game is immediately playable.
* **UI:** Include a simple HUD showing "Current Size" and a "Game Over" overlay with a restart button.

# 4. Code Structure

* Standard Phaser 3 Scene structure: `preload()`, `create()`, and `update()`.
* Clean, commented code so I can swap in my own sprites later.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: No, I generate the sprites separately. Trying to generate a game with sprites in one-shot doesnt seem to be working for me at least

comments.author: Foreign-Quote-53
comments.body:
Well the original is much better looking, but of course that’s not the point of the post. It really is insane how powerful AI had become, especially in game development.

I feel the exact same way where I used to program myself, taught myself fundamentals online, then started watching tutorials… then I started to copy and paste AI code… and now I straight up use Claude code. And it’s insane how good it is.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: Yeah I thought people are just meme'ing with mega prompts but i see the potentials now

replies.author: Foreign-Quote-53
replies.body: Well idk about megaprompts, but just prompts in general. I don’t use megaprompts. Although clearly if the game is simple enough, you can just do one big prompt which is crazy

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body:
Neat! Thanks for sharing the side by side.

AI game dev has been one of the strongest reveals of what’s always been most important in digital apps and games: the little artistic details and the subtle things humans notice that other humans love in experiences. Being able to offload more of the construction work is going to significantly expand the time people have to make digital experiences more expressive and emotionally resonant.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: yeah it basically come down to direction/taste for the art and the gameplay once you can completely remove "construction" from the equation. I am not there yet but my direction/taste aren't exactly great either

comments.author: Beautiful-Arugula-44
comments.body:
"it’s close enough that it feels kind of surreal."  
Huh?! How can one even call this "close" at all?  
I am rather surprised by how different it looks and feels.  
lol

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
I meant mostly just the gameplay. I didn't want a 1:1 remake so I changed it up a bit

\- originally, I wanted to make it completely top-down back in 2023 but I didn't have the right sprites/tileset

\- I also didn't have fully working tanks/soldiers because I was in a game jam at the time (I also didn't know phaser all that well, I just sort of threw something together)

\- gamejam viewers at the time also responded pretty well to the cute graphics but I would have made a "darker" game if I had the option

top-down turned out to be not that great either... so isometric or the pseudo top-down with side scrolling sprites actually may have worked better
